schemes.name: Finite-field Diffie–Hellman
schemes.why: Discrete logarithms with shared public groups: a clear experiment in reusable preparation versus per-instance work.
schemes.spec: Crucible release 6; custom transcript-bound SHA-256 construction.
schemes.correctness: Perfect honest agreement under valid parameters and faithful implementation. Certified primes do not prove hardness.
schemes.gate: Independently review the sampler, KDF and restricted cost model. Keep the custom construction distinct from named FFDHE standards.

schemes.name: RSA encapsulation
schemes.why: Factoring and RSA inversion with fresh moduli, giving a different classical attack setting from either form of DH.
schemes.spec: Crucible release 3; custom generator, encoding and KDF. Not RFC 9690 conformance.
schemes.correctness: Perfect honest agreement conditional on successful valid generation. A generation timeout is a separate availability event.
schemes.gate: Review structured prime generation and the custom KDF; keep any future standardized release and its receipts separate.

schemes.name: DHKEM (X25519)
schemes.why: Fills the elliptic-curve gap with a precisely specified KEM around a widely used primitive.
schemes.spec: RFC 9180 DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), KEM ID 0x0020, base Encaps/Decaps.
schemes.correctness: Honest agreement relies on valid X25519 operations and identical encoding and labeled HKDF context.
schemes.gate: Pin and test an implementation. X25519 is a fixed curve: weakened scalar distributions cannot masquerade as standard tiers.

schemes.name: ML-KEM
schemes.why: The standardized module-lattice baseline, anchoring comparisons to less structured and differently constructed lattice KEMs.
schemes.spec: FIPS 203 (2024), with the published potential corrections inspected; begin with ML-KEM-768 and nest 512/1024.
schemes.correctness: Statistical honest correctness. Analytical failure estimates and executable agreement tests provide different evidence.
schemes.gate: Apply the documented clarifications during conformance work, freeze vectors and source, and implement the admitted failure policy. Three standard sets are not fifty tiers.

schemes.name: FrodoKEM
schemes.why: A plain-LWE comparison: less algebraic structure, with visibly different communication and computation costs.
schemes.spec: Current salted FrodoKEM; public draft-longa-cfrg-frodokem-03 (June 2026), initially 640-SHAKE.
schemes.correctness: Statistical correctness from the declared noise model; successful tests cannot establish the very small tail probability.
schemes.gate: Reconcile the public draft and ISO edition, pin matching code and vectors, and specify key reuse. Do not mix older or ephemeral-use variants.

schemes.name: Streamlined NTRU Prime
schemes.why: An NTRU-style construction and different ring design, with practical relevance through OpenSSH’s hybrid use.
schemes.spec: Round-three specification (2020-10-07), initially sntrup761. NTRU LPRime is a different construction.
schemes.correctness: Designed for perfect honest correctness at admissible parameters. Arithmetic bounds still need checking against the actual adapter.
schemes.gate: Pin and test the implementation and vectors; review admissibility for any reduced profiles. A standalone recovery is not a break of its SSH hybrid.

schemes.name: HQC
schemes.why: A quasi-cyclic code alternative to lattices, with a different decoder and failure-analysis problem from Classic McEliece.
schemes.spec: Team specification dated 2026-10-12, HQC-1/-3/-5. Selected for NIST standardization; this is not a final FIPS conformance claim.
schemes.correctness: Statistical, model-dependent failure analysis. The October revision needs its own probability model and implementation checks.
schemes.gate: The available August 2025 tagged implementation does not establish conformance to October’s changed specification. Resolve this before activation.

schemes.name: Classic McEliece
schemes.why: Hidden Goppa-code structure, exact honest decoding and very different key/ciphertext sizes. Recent structural attacks make it especially informative.
schemes.spec: Team specification dated 2022-10-23; parameter and confirmation variants remain explicit within the page.
schemes.correctness: Perfect honest correctness for valid generation and exact implementation; this does not imply confidentiality or implementation safety.
schemes.gate: Review current attack models and reproduce small-instance evidence before proposing tiers. New published estimates are not full-size practical recoveries.
schemes.caution: Research inclusion, not a deployment recommendation. BSI’s September 29 assessment advises against new deployments while reporting no practical attack on its recommended full-size sets.

deferred.name: Saber
deferred.rationale: A meaningful Module-LWR comparison, deferred because the first three lattice entries add more breadth. First candidate to revisit for a rounding-versus-noise experiment.

deferred.name: Other NTRU constructions
deferred.rationale: NTRU-HPS/HRSS and LPRime are distinct constructions. Add one when a specific comparison justifies another slot; never treat them as aliases of sntrup.

deferred.name: BIKE and rank-metric KEMs
deferred.rationale: BIKE needs a precise decoder/failure review. Rank-metric KEMs are an explicit coverage gap requiring a coherent contemporary construction and implementation.

deferred.name: Hybrids and parameter variants
deferred.rationale: Keep important deployment context and exact profiles inside related pages. Combiners need their own review; every pairing does not need a front-page row.
